qt: to the Commission Ľuboš Blaha (NI) Subject:

The US President has said repeatedly this year that Venezuela’s oil now belongs to the USA. Apparently it was stolen from the USA in the past, but Venezuela is now giving it to the American people as a gift. These statements openly challenge the right of the Venezuelan people to retain the mineral wealth of their own country – in other words, they openly challenge international law. The Commission, including High Representative Kallas herself, have condemned the US violation of international law several times, but they have not moved to impose any sanctions on the USA, despite the fact that the EU has regularly imposed them on other countries. 1.

In order to ensure the EU does not profit economically from activities contrary to the principles of state sovereignty and the permanent sovereignty of nations over their own natural resources, would it not be appropriate here to impose sanctions on the USA – specifically, for example, to ban the import of American fossil fuels (possibly only those originating in Venezuela), in a manner akin to the decision to ban energy imports from Russia when the EU judged Russia’s actions to be in violation of international law?
What objective criteria does the Commission apply when deciding whether a violation of international law justifies a proposal to adopt restrictive measures?

How will the Commission ensure its sanctions policy is applied consistently and impartially, irrespective of which state carried out the action the EU considers to be a violation of international law?
